skills.name: navigate
skills.description: Plan and follow a path to a target location or pose. Use location names from the world vocabulary (e.g., pantry, fridge, table). The robot will automatically navigate to the appropriate position for interacting with objects at that location.

skills.name: pick
skills.description: Pick up an object at the current location. The robot must be at a location where the object is present. Use object names or categories from the world vocabulary. CONSTRAINT - Single-arm robot can only hold one object at a time; cannot pick while already holding something.

skills.name: place
skills.description: Place the currently held object at the current location. The robot must be at a location where objects can be placed (navigate to a location first).

skills.name: detect
skills.description: Detect objects at the current location. The robot must be at a location (navigate there first). If the location can be closed (e.g., pantry, fridge), it must be opened first using the open action. The object parameter can be a specific object name or category from the world vocabulary.

skills.name: open
skills.description: Open the current location or target location if provided. Certain locations like pantry and fridge must be opened before you can detect or pick objects inside them. CONSTRAINT - Cannot open while holding an object (single-arm robot).

skills.name: close
skills.description: Close the current location or target location if provided. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT - Cannot close while holding an object (single-arm robot). Only close locations when NOT holding anything. If you pick an object from a location, do NOT close it until after you place the object elsewhere.

notes: Top-level BT JSON must include a `root` object.
Memory rule: set memory=true on any sequence/selector that contains action nodes, so completed actions are not re-run on subsequent ticks.
Use memory=false only for purely reactive condition/sensor chains that should re-evaluate from the start every tick.

rootstocks.name: detect_pick
rootstocks.description: Canonical detect-gated manipulation pattern for direct pick tasks.
rootstocks.when_to_use: Use when the task is to go to one location, verify the target object, and pick it.

slots.object_query: Object name or category to detect and pick.
slots.source_location: Location or object spawn to navigate to before detect and pick.
slots.open_before_detect: Set true when the source location can be closed, such as pantry or fridge.

rootstocks.anti_pattern: Do not pick before detect succeeds. Do not close a container while holding an object: this robot is single-arm, so open and close both require an empty gripper and fail at runtime otherwise, aborting the task. Close only if the task asks for the container to end closed, and then only after the object has been placed.

rootstocks.description: Two-branch selector search pattern with a guarded detect-and-pick branch at each location.
rootstocks.when_to_use: Use when the task says to search one location, then fall back to a second location, and pick the object if found.

slots.object_query: Object name or category to detect and pick.
slots.primary_open_before_detect: Set true when the primary location can be closed.
slots.fallback_open_before_detect: Set true when the fallback location can be closed.

rootstocks.anti_pattern: Do not make the fallback branch a blind navigate-and-pick sequence. Do not close a container while holding an object: close requires an empty gripper on this single-arm robot and fails at runtime. Close only if the task asks for it, and then only after the object has been placed.

rootstocks.name: search_pick_deliver
rootstocks.description: Search with selector fallback, then continue to a delivery step such as place or return.
rootstocks.when_to_use: Use when the task says to search across candidate locations and then either place the object somewhere or return to a destination while holding it.

slots.object_query: Object name or category to detect and pick.
slots.primary_open_before_detect: Set true when the primary location can be closed.
slots.fallback_open_before_detect: Set true when the fallback location can be closed.

rootstocks.anti_pattern: Do not put delivery actions inside only one selector branch. Do not open or close any container while holding an object: both require an empty gripper on this single-arm robot and fail at runtime. If the destination is a container that must be opened, open it before picking the object. Close only if the task asks for it, and then only after placing.

rootstocks.name: retrieve_and_restore
rootstocks.description: Retrieve an object from a closeable container, deliver it, then restore the container to closed.
rootstocks.when_to_use: Use when the task asks for the container to end closed -- "close the fridge", "leave it as you found it", "put it back the way it was". If the task does not ask for that, use detect_pick or search_pick_deliver and leave the container open.

slots.object_query: Object name or category to detect and pick.
slots.source_location: Container holding the object, which must end closed.
slots.destination_location: Where the object must end up.

rootstocks.anti_pattern: Do not close the container immediately after picking. This robot is single-arm: close requires an empty gripper, so closing while still holding the object fails at runtime and aborts the task. The gripper is free only after place, which is why the close comes last and needs a navigate back to the container.

skills.name: NavigateToLocation
skills.description: Navigates the robot to a named place (e.g. "lab", "front_door") defined in the server's locations YAML file. Use list_world_entities to see available location names. Returns SUCCESS when the robot arrives, FAILURE if the location is unknown or navigation fails.

skills.name: Spin
skills.description: Rotates the robot in place by a given angle. Returns SUCCESS when the target yaw is reached, FAILURE on timeout or error. Use 6.28 for a full 360° scan, 3.14 for 180°.

skills.name: Wait
skills.description: Pauses the robot in place for a specified duration. Returns SUCCESS after the duration elapses, FAILURE on error.

skills.name: WaitForDetection
skills.description: Blocks the behavior tree until an object of the specified class is detected with sufficient confidence, then returns SUCCESS. If a timeout is set and no detection arrives within that window, returns FAILURE. Use this to gate downstream actions on perception (e.g. "wait until a person is seen, then navigate to them"). Set timeout="0.0" (default) to wait indefinitely.

skills.name: CheckDetection
skills.description: Condition node (level-triggered): returns SUCCESS if a matching detection has been received within the last max_age seconds, FAILURE otherwise. SUCCESS holds across multiple ticks while detections are arriving within the time window (default 2.0s). This makes it robust to detection sources running slower than the BT tick rate (e.g. 1 Hz vision with a 10 Hz tree). Designed for use inside ReactiveFallback (or ReactiveSequence) so the condition is re-evaluated every tick alongside a long-running action — the canonical "do X until detected" pattern. Do NOT place inside Parallel: Parallel latches a child's first FAILURE for the rest of the round, so the watch will silently stop firing.

skills.name: MoveForward
skills.description: Drives the robot forward along its current heading a set distance. Returns SUCCESS when the target distance is reached, FAILURE on timeout or error. Useful for precise short-distance forward movements.

skills.name: BackUp
skills.description: Reverses the robot a set distance. Returns SUCCESS when the target distance is reached, FAILURE on timeout or error. Useful for recovery after getting stuck or before retrying navigation.

skills.name: HeadingController
skills.description: Yaws the robot in place to keep its camera aligned with a detected object of the given class. Returns SUCCESS once the target is centered. Returns FAILURE when no detection arrives for detection_loss_timeout seconds (default 1.0s), or when the overall timeout fires. IMPORTANT — this node returns SUCCESS as soon as alignment is achieved and then stops. It does NOT loop. It also returns FAILURE when the detection is lost for more than detection_loss_timeout seconds (default 1.0s). For continuous tracking, two things must happen together: 1. Wrap HeadingController in KeepRunningUntilFailure so each SUCCESS (aligned) is converted back to RUNNING and tracking resumes. 2. Place the wrapped node under a parent that ABSORBS the eventual detection-loss FAILURE — otherwise the FAILURE cascades up through any enclosing Sequence / KeepRunningUntilFailure and ends the mission. The canonical safe form is ReactiveSequence(CheckDetection, KRUF(HeadingController)) placed inside a ReactiveFallback that switches to other behavior when no person is seen: <ReactiveFallback> <ReactiveSequence name="face_if_person"> <CheckDetection class_name="person" min_confidence="0.5"/> <KeepRunningUntilFailure> <HeadingController class_name="person" timeout="0.0" detection_loss_timeout="1.0"/> </KeepRunningUntilFailure> </ReactiveSequence> <!-- When no person: do something else (sweep, patrol, idle, etc.) --> ... </ReactiveFallback> See rootstocks sweep_face_loop and patrol_with_detection_resume for complete examples. DO NOT use bare KeepRunningUntilFailure(HeadingController) as a phase inside a looping Sequence — the detection-loss FAILURE will propagate through the Sequence and the outer KeepRunningUntilFailure and terminate the mission. Use bare (without the decorator) only when you want one-shot alignment before proceeding to the next step (e.g. "face the person, then drive forward").

operators.name: Sequence
operators.description: Executes children left-to-right. Returns FAILURE on the first child that fails, SUCCESS if all children succeed. Use for ordered steps that must all complete.

operators.name: Fallback
operators.description: Tries children left-to-right. Returns SUCCESS on the first child that succeeds, FAILURE if all children fail. Use to express "try A, if that fails try B".

operators.name: Parallel
operators.description: Ticks children every BT tick. Returns SUCCESS when success_count children have succeeded; returns FAILURE when failure_count children have failed. RUNNING children do not count toward either threshold.

operators.name: ReactiveFallback
operators.description: Like Fallback (ticks children left-to-right, returns SUCCESS on first child that succeeds), but re-ticks earlier-FAILURE children every BT tick. When a later child is RUNNING and an earlier child returns SUCCESS, the running child is halted and ReactiveFallback returns SUCCESS. PRIMARY USE CASE — run an action while continuously watching a condition: <ReactiveFallback> <CheckDetection class_name="person" .../> <!-- watched every tick --> <KeepRunningUntilFailure> <Spin .../> <!-- runs until detection fires --> </KeepRunningUntilFailure> </ReactiveFallback> On every tick CheckDetection is re-evaluated. While it returns FAILURE, the spin action keeps running. The instant it returns SUCCESS, the spin is halted and the whole ReactiveFallback returns SUCCESS. This is the correct pattern for "do X until condition Y" — NOT Parallel.

operators.name: ReactiveSequence
operators.description: Like Sequence (ticks children left-to-right, returns FAILURE on first failure, SUCCESS when all succeed), but re-ticks earlier-SUCCESS children every BT tick. When a later child is RUNNING and an earlier child returns FAILURE, the running child is halted and ReactiveSequence returns FAILURE. Use for "run an action only while precondition holds": the precondition is the first child (Condition node), and the action follows. If the precondition flips to FAILURE mid-action, the action is interrupted.

operators.name: Inverter
operators.description: Decorator with exactly one child. Inverts SUCCESS to FAILURE and vice versa. RUNNING stays RUNNING. WARNING — error propagation: Inverter also inverts FAILURE from hardware errors into SUCCESS. Never wrap a fallible action node in Inverter expecting to loop it — use KeepRunningUntilFailure instead. Inverter is safe for condition nodes (CheckDetection) whose FAILURE is semantic (meaning "not detected"), not an error.

operators.name: KeepRunningUntilFailure
operators.description: Decorator with exactly one child. Returns RUNNING when the child returns SUCCESS, and FAILURE when the child returns FAILURE. RUNNING passes through as RUNNING. PRIMARY USE CASE — looping an action indefinitely until an error or external halt: <KeepRunningUntilFailure> <Spin target_yaw="6.28" .../> </KeepRunningUntilFailure> When Spin completes a rotation (SUCCESS), KeepRunningUntilFailure returns RUNNING, causing the parent to tick it again on the next cycle — Spin restarts. When Spin fails, FAILURE propagates up normally. IMPORTANT: Do NOT use Inverter+RetryUntilSuccessful to loop actions. When the action fails, Inverter converts FAILURE→SUCCESS, and RetryUntilSuccessful exits immediately with SUCCESS — the entire tree short-circuits. KeepRunningUntilFailure is the correct and safe looping decorator.

operators.name: Repeat
operators.description: Retries its child up to num_cycles times, counting only SUCCESS results. If the child fails, Repeat returns FAILURE immediately (it does not retry on failure). Use num_cycles="-1" for infinite repetition (child must not fail). To loop until external halt regardless of child result, use KeepRunningUntilFailure.

operators.name: RetryUntilSuccessful
operators.description: Retries its child up to num_attempts times until the child returns SUCCESS. Returns FAILURE if all attempts are exhausted without SUCCESS. WARNING: Use only when you genuinely want to retry on FAILURE. Do NOT combine with Inverter to loop an action — when the action fails, Inverter converts FAILURE→SUCCESS, RetryUntilSuccessful exits immediately with SUCCESS, and the tree short-circuits silently. Use KeepRunningUntilFailure for looping actions.

operators.name: AlwaysSuccess
operators.description: Leaf node that always returns SUCCESS. Use inside a Fallback as the last branch to prevent FAILURE from propagating upward (graceful degradation).

operators.name: ForceSuccess
operators.description: Decorator that converts any child result to SUCCESS. RUNNING passes through. Use to make optional steps in a Sequence non-blocking.

operators.name: ForceFailure
operators.description: Decorator that converts any child result to FAILURE. RUNNING passes through.

operators.name: SequenceWithMemory
operators.description: Like Sequence (left-to-right, FAILURE on first child failure, SUCCESS when all succeed), but preserves its child index across halt() calls. When the node is halted by a parent (e.g. a ReactiveFallback interrupting a patrol on detection), it remembers which child was running. On the next tick it resumes from that child rather than restarting from child 0. PRIMARY USE CASE — interruptible patrol that resumes from the interrupted waypoint: <ReactiveFallback> <ReactiveSequence> <CheckDetection class_name="person" min_confidence="0.5"/> <HeadingController class_name="person" timeout="0.0"/> </ReactiveSequence> <KeepRunningUntilFailure> <SequenceWithMemory name="patrol_loop"> <NavigateToLocation location="location_a"/> <NavigateToLocation location="location_b"/> <NavigateToLocation location="location_c"/> </SequenceWithMemory> </KeepRunningUntilFailure> </ReactiveFallback> When a person is detected mid-patrol, the patrol is halted. When the person leaves and patrol resumes, SequenceWithMemory continues from the interrupted waypoint rather than restarting at location_a. Use plain Sequence when restart-from-beginning on interruption is acceptable or desired (e.g. a single-pass patrol with no reactive interrupts).

operators.name: RunOnce
operators.description: Decorator with exactly one child. Ticks the child only on the first execution; on all subsequent ticks it returns the cached result without re-ticking the child. PRIMARY USE CASE — one-shot initialization before a repeating loop: <KeepRunningUntilFailure> <Sequence> <RunOnce> <NavigateToLocation location="home_base"/> </RunOnce> <NavigateToLocation location="location_a"/> <NavigateToLocation location="location_b"/> </Sequence> </KeepRunningUntilFailure> The robot drives to home_base only on the first loop pass, then skips it on every subsequent pass while continuing to patrol location_a and location_b. RunOnce resets only if the entire subtree is halted by a parent node. Do NOT use RunOnce to guard an action that should re-run after an interruption — use plain Sequence ordering instead.

rootstocks.name: patrol_locations
rootstocks.description: Drive through a fixed list of named locations, optionally indefinitely.
rootstocks.prose:
To patrol a fixed list of named locations once, chain NavigateToLocation calls inside a Sequence:

  <Sequence>
    <NavigateToLocation location="location_a"/>
    <NavigateToLocation location="location_b"/>
    <NavigateToLocation location="location_c"/>
  </Sequence>

To patrol indefinitely, wrap the Sequence in KeepRunningUntilFailure. The sequence completes one full pass (SUCCESS), which the decorator converts to RUNNING so the next tick restarts the sequence:

  <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
    <Sequence>
      <NavigateToLocation location="location_a"/>
      <NavigateToLocation location="location_b"/>
    </Sequence>
  </KeepRunningUntilFailure>

rootstocks.name: loop_action_until_detection
rootstocks.description: Loop an action (e.g. Spin) until a target object is detected, then stop.
rootstocks.prose:
To loop an action (e.g. Spin) until an object is detected, use ReactiveFallback with KeepRunningUntilFailure. Never use Parallel for this.
CORRECT:
  <ReactiveFallback>
    <CheckDetection class_name="person" min_confidence="0.5"/>
    <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
      <Spin target_yaw="6.28" time_allowance="15.0"/>
    </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
  </ReactiveFallback>

ReactiveFallback re-ticks CheckDetection every cycle. While it returns FAILURE, the spin keeps running. When it returns SUCCESS, the spin is halted and the tree exits SUCCESS. KeepRunningUntilFailure ensures each completed Spin rotation restarts rather than ending the tree.

rootstocks.name: patrol_until_detection
rootstocks.description: Patrol named locations indefinitely until a target object is detected.
rootstocks.prose:
To patrol named locations until an object is detected, place a CheckDetection inside a ReactiveFallback alongside the patrol Sequence wrapped in KeepRunningUntilFailure:

  <ReactiveFallback>
    <CheckDetection class_name="person" min_confidence="0.5"/>
    <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
      <Sequence>
        <NavigateToLocation location="location_a"/>
        <NavigateToLocation location="location_b"/>
      </Sequence>
    </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
  </ReactiveFallback>

On detection, the patrol is halted and ReactiveFallback returns SUCCESS. Do NOT use Parallel here — CheckDetection's first FAILURE would latch and the watch would never fire again.

rootstocks.name: continuous_tracking
rootstocks.description: Continuously face a detected person via HeadingController with safe failure handling.
rootstocks.prose:
HeadingController returns SUCCESS when the target is centered — it does NOT loop on its own. It also returns FAILURE when the detection is lost for more than detection_loss_timeout seconds (default 1.0s).
For continuous tracking, two things must happen together:
  1. Wrap HeadingController in KeepRunningUntilFailure so each SUCCESS (aligned) is
     converted back to RUNNING and tracking resumes.
  2. Place the wrapped node under a parent that ABSORBS the eventual detection-loss
     FAILURE — otherwise the FAILURE cascades up through any enclosing Sequence /
     KeepRunningUntilFailure and ends the mission.

The canonical safe form is ReactiveSequence(CheckDetection, KRUF(HeadingController)) placed inside a ReactiveFallback that switches to other behavior when no person is seen:

  <ReactiveFallback>
    <ReactiveSequence name="face_if_person">
      <CheckDetection class_name="person" min_confidence="0.5"/>
      <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
        <HeadingController class_name="person" timeout="0.0" detection_loss_timeout="1.0"/>
      </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
    </ReactiveSequence>
    <!-- When no person: do something else (sweep, patrol, idle, etc.) -->
    ...
  </ReactiveFallback>

CheckDetection guards entry into the tracking branch and halts it when the detection drops; HeadingController's detection_loss_timeout is a second safety net. Either way the ReactiveFallback falls through cleanly to the next branch and no FAILURE escapes upward. See rootstocks sweep_face_loop and patrol_with_detection_resume for complete examples.
DO NOT use bare KeepRunningUntilFailure(HeadingController) as a phase inside a looping Sequence — the detection-loss FAILURE will propagate through the Sequence and the outer KeepRunningUntilFailure and terminate the mission.
Use bare HeadingController (no decorator) only for one-shot alignment before a subsequent action:

  <Sequence>
    <HeadingController name="face_person" class_name="person" timeout="5.0"/>
    <MoveForward forward_dist="1.0"/>
  </Sequence>

rootstocks.name: patrol_with_detection_resume
rootstocks.description: Patrol indefinitely; pause to face a detected person; resume patrol from interrupted waypoint.
rootstocks.prose:
To patrol indefinitely and resume from the interrupted waypoint (not from the start) after a reactive event (e.g. stopping to face a detected person), use SequenceWithMemory for the patrol loop instead of plain Sequence.
Plain Sequence resets its child index to 0 when halted — so patrol always restarts from the first waypoint after an interruption. SequenceWithMemory preserves the index across halts, resuming from the waypoint that was interrupted.

  <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
    <ReactiveFallback>
      <ReactiveSequence>
        <CheckDetection class_name="person" min_confidence="0.5"/>
        <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
          <HeadingController class_name="person" timeout="0.0"/>
        </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
      </ReactiveSequence>
      <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
        <SequenceWithMemory name="patrol_loop">
          <NavigateToLocation location="location_a"/>
          <NavigateToLocation location="location_b"/>
          <NavigateToLocation location="location_c"/>
        </SequenceWithMemory>
      </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
    </ReactiveFallback>
  </KeepRunningUntilFailure>

How termination works: CheckDetection holds SUCCESS across ticks while the person is present (max_age window, default 2.0s). When the person leaves, CheckDetection returns FAILURE after the window expires, which halts HeadingController via ReactiveSequence. HeadingController also returns FAILURE independently after detection_loss_timeout (1.0s default), providing a second safety net. Either way, the ReactiveFallback falls through to resume patrol.
Use plain Sequence instead when restarting the patrol from the beginning after any interruption is acceptable (simpler and marginally more predictable).

rootstocks.name: sweep_face_loop
rootstocks.description: Sweep in place until a person is detected; face them until they leave; resume sweeping indefinitely.
rootstocks.prose:
To loop a stationary action (e.g. Spin to sweep in place) and reactively switch to facing a detected person, then resume the action when the person leaves — use a ReactiveFallback inside KeepRunningUntilFailure:

  <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
    <ReactiveFallback>
      <ReactiveSequence name="face_if_person">
        <CheckDetection class_name="person" min_confidence="0.5"/>
        <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
          <HeadingController class_name="person" timeout="0.0" detection_loss_timeout="1.0"/>
        </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
      </ReactiveSequence>
      <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
        <Spin target_yaw="6.28" time_allowance="15.0"/>
      </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
    </ReactiveFallback>
  </KeepRunningUntilFailure>

Structurally identical to patrol_with_detection_resume, except the idle branch is a looped Spin instead of a SequenceWithMemory of NavigateToLocation. Use when there is no patrol route — just a stationary watch point with reactive person-facing.
The outer KeepRunningUntilFailure absorbs all FAILUREs from inside, so neither HeadingController's detection-loss nor a single failed Spin rotation will terminate the mission — the loop just continues into the next phase.
DO NOT replace this structure with a Sequence-of-phases (Sweep, then Face) wrapped in KeepRunningUntilFailure. HeadingController's detection-loss FAILURE would cascade up through the Sequence and end the mission.

rootstocks.description: Block until an object is detected (or timeout), then perform a follow-up action.
rootstocks.prose:
To block until an object is seen then perform an action, use WaitForDetection in a Sequence. WaitForDetection holds RUNNING until the class appears, then returns SUCCESS so the Sequence proceeds to the next child.

  <Sequence>
    <WaitForDetection class_name="person" timeout="30.0"/>
    <NavigateToLocation location="lab"/>
  </Sequence>
